deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X over S, and Mod(X/S), the category of O_X-modules whose morphisms are differential operators. Earlier pages define, for M in Mod(X/S), a cosimplicial object O^*[M]. Morphisms D: M -> N are realized as O_X-linear maps O^*[M] -> O^*[N]; this is the linearization of differential operators.

Section 4 on the previous page gives an equivalent construction. Take the formal completions X^{[i]} of the diagonal in (X/S)^{i+1}. Together with their projections and diagonals they form a simplicial formal prescheme over X, of the shape X^{[2]} => X^{[1]} -> X^{[0]} = X. Its rings of functions give a cosimplicial ring Q^* (the 'anneau simplicial' / cristallin). For the i-th level this is the ring of principal parts of infinite order P^∞ of X^{i+1}/S along the diagonal. Set Q^*[M] = Q^* ⊗_{O_X} M, with M tensored via one projection.

The key point on this page is that X^{[1]} -> X^{[0]} admits a section, the diagonal. So the augmented cosimplicial module M -> Q^0[M] => Q^1[M] ... has an extra codegeneracy. It is therefore homotopically trivial, i.e. Q^*[M] is a resolution of M. The contracting homotopy is linear only for the 'exterior' O_X-structures coming from the untouched factors, which is why he insists on 'mettant bien les structures extérieures'.

Grothendieck then flags two caveats.
- In what sense 'resolution' is meant, since the Q^i[M] are really pro-objects (inverse systems Q^i_{(n)} ⊗ M). He asks whether Artin–Rees pro-modules form an abelian category.
- Whether M must be quasi-coherent.

His conclusion: work at finite level n (truncated neighbourhoods), then pass to lim. This gives that ℓQ^*[M] = lim_n Q^*[M]_{(n)} is a resolution of M when M is quasi-coherent.

The next page uses this to compute H^*(X,M) as the hypercohomology of ℓQ^*[M], with a spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(i ↦ H^q(X^{[i+1]}, M)). It also extends the construction to complexes of differential operators in D^+(X/S). This is the formal 'Čech–Alexander' / linearization resolution underlying the comparison of infinitesimal (and crystalline) cohomology with de Rham-type complexes.
errors: No real mathematical error. The extra-degeneracy argument gives exactness only for the correct choice of O_X-structure (he notes this). Exactness of the limit needs quasi-coherence plus Mittag-Leffler / Artin–Rees control (he notes this too). Indexing is loose: the next page corrects X^{(i+1)} = (X/S)^{i+2}, so there is an off-by-one between [i] and the number of factors.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial ring of formal neighbourhoods of diagonals (principal parts of infinite order) and Q^*[M] = Q^* ⊗ M as a resolution of M, proved via the section given by the diagonal (extra degeneracy).
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander / linearization resolution; infinitesimal Čech complex; Grothendieck–Berthelot linearization of differential operators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966/68); Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974); Berthelot–Ogus (1978); later Bhatt–de Jong (Čech–Alexander complexes)
ideas.where_published: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), §4 (Čech computation of infinitesimal cohomology); EGA IV 16.8 for principal parts / linearization

ideas.what: Mod(X/S): modules with differential operators as morphisms, embedded O_X-linearly via M ↦ Q^*[M]; extension to D^+(Mod(X/S)).
ideas.modern_name: Category of differential complexes and its linearization into (pro-)crystals / D-modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Berthelot (1974); Herrera–Lieberman; M. Saito (1989, induced D-modules and differential complexes)
ideas.where_published: Partially in the Crystals paper / EGA IV 16.8; the derived category D^+(X/S) of differential complexes is developed later by others

ideas.what: Question whether Artin–Rees pro-modules form an abelian category.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the standard linearization / Čech–Alexander resolution by formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal, which is in Grothendieck's own Crystals exposé and in Berthelot's thesis. The technical caveats (AR pro-modules, quasi-coherence) were all later resolved in the literature. Nothing appears beyond the published record.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the ring is written Q^* (not O^*); the insertion above reads something like 'simplicial', giving 'l'anneau simplicial Q^*', rather than 'cristallin'.
'Comme X^{[1]} a une section sur X^{[0]}' (not 'est une section'); the superscripts are hatted [1], [0] (formal neighbourhoods).
'Il faut cependant préciser le sens qu'on attache à cette expression'.
Last lines: '...débutant par une [?] et passant à la limite aux lim ..., on trouve que ℓQ^*[M] est une résolution de M si M quasi-coh.' The 'ℓ' (limit) before Q^*[M] is present in the image.
